text: Ravelin Point, May 14 — The Sennet Lighthouse was decommissioned in 1987 after inspectors deemed its lantern system too costly to maintain, people familiar with the matter said. The tower, on the outer edge of Ravelin Point’s north breakwater, had operated for 73 years before the Harbor Works Authority shuttered the beacon and transferred its fog-signal duties to an automated mast nearby. Records cited by the people said the final lamp was extinguished on Nov. 3, 1987, at 11:40 p.m., during a scheduled weather lull. The granite structure remains standing and is now used for occasional equipment storage, while public access has been restricted since a 2019 safety review.
